conversation.Statement: Hello, is this Mrs. Barnes? My name is Tracy, I'm calling from Amazon's Account Security Team. I hope you're doing well today. I'm reaching out regarding an urgent matter with your Amazon account.
Yes, this is Helen Barnes. Is there a problem with my account?

Thank you, Mrs. Barnes. I know these calls can be unsettling, but I want to assure you I'm here to help. We noticed some unusual activity on your Amazon account, an attempt to purchase a MacBook Pro for $2,499. I want to make sure you authorized this.
Oh no, I definitely didn't buy a MacBook. I don't even know how to use one!

I completely understand, and you're not alone, these things happen. To protect your account, I need to confirm some details with you and help cancel that order before it ships. Could you please verify your email address linked to Amazon for me?
It should be h.barnes1948@gmail.com, I think.
Perfect, thank you. Now, to ensure I'm speaking with the account holder, could you also confirm your full mailing address?
It's 52 Oak Lane, Riverwood, NY 11784.

Thank you, Mrs. Barnes. Everything matches our records. I want to reassure you that we're taking this very seriously. Unfortunately, because the suspicious order is pending shipment, we have to act quickly to stop it and secure your funds.
This is all so much. My husband used to handle these things. He passed away last month, so I'm not very good with computers.

I am truly sorry for your loss, Mrs. Barnes. I promise I'll walk you through each step, and you're in safe hands. Now, to prevent the fraudulent charge, Amazon policy requires a quick verification through our secure refund portal. Do you have access to a computer or smartphone right now?
Yes, I have my iPad here.
That's perfect. Can you please open the Safari browser and go to www.AmazonHelpVerify.com? This is Amazon's secure portal for handling urgent account issues.
Alright, I'm there. It says I need a support code.
Great. I'll generate that for you now. Your support code is 4582. Enter that and click 'Start'.
Okay, I put it in. Now it's asking me to log in with my Amazon password.
That's right, it's just to confirm your identity and let us block the fraudulent order. Please enter your Amazon password. If you're unsure, I can wait while you look it up.
I think it's Helen1950!, with a capital H.

Thank you. It's verifying now. I'm so glad you caught this in time, it'll help me make sure everything is safe. Now, it appears the MacBook order was placed using a payment from your checking account ending in 2176. Is that correct?
Yes, that matches my account.

Okay, I'm flagging the order as unauthorized. To finalize the cancellation and process your refund, Amazon's system requires you to verify a refundable deposit. This is purely a technical step due to new anti-fraud policies, I know it sounds odd, but it's to protect you and me. I could lose my job if this isn't done properly.
I don't understand. What do you need me to do?

You'll receive instructions on your iPad in a moment. It's going to ask you to purchase Amazon gift cards totaling $2,500, the same amount as the unauthorized order. You won't lose any money; once you send the codes, the system verifies your identity, cancels the fraudulent transaction, and refunds the full amount back to your account. I'll stay with you through the process.
So I have to actually buy gift cards? I'm on a fixed income since my husband passed.

I completely understand, Mrs. Barnes. Please know that this is only temporary, and I'll make sure you're not out any money. Once we verify, the refund posts to your bank within 2 hours. It's just Amazon's strict security measure because of the account breach.
Alright, I guess. Can I do it online?

Absolutely. You can purchase the gift cards online at Amazon.com. Please select five cards of $500 each, and I'll guide you step by step. When you have the codes, let me know, and I'll submit them to our refund system.
Okay, I'm buying them now. It's making me sign in again.
That's normal. Please proceed, and let me know if you need help with any step. I truly appreciate your patience. Remember, this is just to protect you and get your money back.
Alright, I've got the emails with the gift card codes.
Perfect. Please read each code to me, one at a time, so I can enter them into Amazon's refund portal and process your reimbursement.
The first code is XJ7P-92KD-LM4Q-FG2T.
Great, thank you. Now the next one, please.
The second is MZ3Q-P5KL-8WTY-6V9S.
Thank you, Mrs. Barnes. You're doing exactly right. Please continue with the next code.
Here's the third: R5KL-2V8N-GT6Q-WZPX.
Almost done. Two more codes, please.
Fourth is H29K-7M8T-QPX4-LVRP.
Thank you, and whenever you're ready, the last code.
The last one is Q5NL-7P8K-9LMW-3XZJ.

Excellent work, Mrs. Barnes. I've entered all the codes. The system is now processing your refund. You should see the $2,500 returned to your bank within two hours. I know this was stressful, but you handled it perfectly. Thank you for trusting me to help.
Thank you for helping me. I hope this never happens again.
You're very welcome. If you have any more questions, you can always call Amazon's support line. Take care of yourself, Mrs. Barnes.
